'''Hugo González Peña''' (born 5 February 2006) is a Spanish professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Boston Celtics]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).<ref name="NBAprofile">{{Cite web |title=Hugo González |url=https://www.nba.com/stats/player/1642864 |access-date=11 July 2026 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

==Early life and career==
González was born in [[Madrid]] to parents who both played professional basketball in Spain. He began playing basketball at age nine with an academy in [[San Agustín del Guadalix]], where his father, Paco, had played near the end of his career. González spent three years with the academy before joining [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]]'s youth system in the 2017–18 season.<ref name="FIBAfeature">{{Cite web |last=Rissotto |first=Ignacio |date=28 May 2025 |title=Next Big Thing: Hugo Gonzalez leading Spain's next generation |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-eurobasket-2025/news/next-big-thing-hugo-gonzalez-leading-spains-next-generation |access-date=11 July 2026 |website=FIBA.basketball}}</ref><ref name="RealMadridFarewell">{{Cite web |date=30 June 2025 |title=Official Announcement: Hugo González |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-hugo-gonzalez-30-06-2025 |access-date=11 July 2026 |website=Real Madrid CF}}</ref>

González progressed through Real Madrid's academy and played for its junior and reserve teams while beginning to make appearances for the senior team. In 2023, he helped Real Madrid's under-18 team win the [[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]]. The team retained the title in 2024, when González was named the tournament's most valuable player. He scored 23 points and recorded six assists in the championship game against U18 PFBB INSEP Paris and averaged 17.5 points, 6.5 rebounds and 3.8 assists during the tournament.<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 May 2024 |title=Gonzalez crowned MVP after helping Real to repeat title |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/nge/news/gonzalez-crowned-mvp-after-helping-real-to-repeat-title/ |access-date=11 July 2026 |website=Euroleague Basketball}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Real Madrid (2022–2025)===
On 2 October 2022, González made his first-team and [[Liga ACB]] debut for Real Madrid against [[Obradoiro CAB|Monbus Obradoiro]]. He played three minutes and eight seconds, scoring four points and recording a [[Performance Index Rating|PIR]] of five in a Real Madrid victory. At 16 years, seven months and 27 days old, he became the fourth-youngest Real Madrid player to appear in the ACB.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2 October 2022 |title=Hugo González makes his Real Madrid debut |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/basket/first-team/press-conference/hugo-gonzalez-makes-his-real-madrid-debut |access-date=11 July 2026 |website=Real Madrid CF}}</ref>

González became part of Real Madrid's senior rotation during the 2024–25 season and was selected to the All-Liga ACB Young Players Team. During his first-team career, he won the [[Supercopa de España de Baloncesto|Spanish Super Cup]] in 2023, the [[Copa del Rey de Baloncesto|Copa del Rey]] in 2024 and consecutive Liga ACB championships in 2024 and 2025. Real Madrid announced his departure from the club on 30 June 2025.<ref name="RealMadridFarewell" />

===Boston Celtics (2025–present)===
On 25 June 2025, González was selected by the [[Boston Celtics]] with the 28th overall pick in the [[2025 NBA draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=NBA 2025 Draft Prospects: Hugo González |url=https://www.nba.com/draft/2025/prospects/hugo-gonzalez |access-date=11 July 2026 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He signed his rookie-scale contract with Boston on 1 July and subsequently joined the Celtics' roster for the [[2025 NBA Summer League]] in [[Las Vegas]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=1 July 2025 |title=Celtics sign rookie Hugo Gonzalez as new draftees get their first taste of Boston |url=https://www.bostonsportsjournal.com/2025/07/01/celtics-sign-rookie-hugo-gonzalez-as-new-draftees-get-their-first-taste-of-boston |access-date=11 July 2026 |work=Boston Sports Journal}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=8 July 2025 |title=Celtics announce NBA Summer League 2025 roster |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/celtics-announce-nba-summer-league-2025-roster |access-date=11 July 2026 |website=Boston Celtics}}</ref>

González made his NBA debut on 24 October 2025 against the [[New York Knicks]], recording six points, four rebounds, one assist and two steals in a 105–95 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 October 2025 |title=Boston Celtics vs New York Knicks Oct 24, 2025 Box Scores |url=https://www.nba.com/game/bos-vs-nyk-0022500018/box-score |access-date=11 July 2026 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He made his first NBA start two days later against the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 October 2025 |title=Celtics' Hugo Gonzalez: Scoreless in first start |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/celtics-hugo-gonzalez-scoreless-in-first-start/ |access-date=11 July 2026 |website=CBS Sports}}</ref>

On 20 December, González recorded his first NBA double-double, finishing with 10 points, 10 rebounds, two steals and one block in a 112–96 victory over the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=21 December 2025 |title=Celtics' Hugo Gonzalez: First double-double of NBA career |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/celtics-hugo-gonzalez-first-double-double-of-nba-career/ |access-date=11 July 2026 |website=CBS Sports}}</ref> On 23 January 2026, he made a corner three-pointer with four-tenths of a second remaining in the first overtime period to force a second overtime against the [[Brooklyn Nets]]. Boston won the game 130–126.<ref>{{Cite news |date=24 January 2026 |title=Celtics survive poor regulation finish to beat Nets in double OT |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/basketball/celtics-survive-poor-regulation-finish-beat-nets-double-ot--flm-2026-01-24/ |access-date=11 July 2026 |work=Reuters}}</ref>

On 2 March, González recorded career highs of 18 points and 16 rebounds, along with three steals and two blocks, in a 108–81 victory over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goss |first=Nick |last2=Hartwell |first2=Darren |date=2 March 2026 |title=Celtics-Bucks recap: Hugo Gonzalez dominates as C's extend win streak |url=https://www.nbcsportsboston.com/nba/boston-celtics/live-updates-highlights-score-bucksgiannis-antetokounmpo/773673/ |access-date=11 July 2026 |website=NBC Sports Boston}}</ref> He finished his rookie regular season averaging 3.9 points and 3.3 rebounds over 74 games, including three starts.<ref name="NBAprofile" />

==National team career==

===Junior teams===
In July 2022, González played for Spain at the [[2022 FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup]] in [[Málaga]], helping the team win the silver medal after losing the final to the United States.<ref name="FIBAfeature" />

In July 2023, he won a silver medal at the [[2023 FIBA U18 European Championship]] in [[Niš]], Serbia, where Spain lost the final to the host team.<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 July 2023 |title=Topic, Bosnjakovic outduel Mara and Co as Serbia dethrone Spain |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/news/europe-u18-2023-news-hosts-serbia-down-back-to-back-champs-spain-celebrate-return-to-top-of-podium |access-date=11 July 2026 |website=FIBA.basketball}}</ref> González was selected to the tournament's All-Star Five after averaging 14.3 points, 6.6 rebounds and 1.7 assists per game.<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 July 2023 |title=Serbia star Topic takes home MVP award |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/news/europe-u18-2023-news-serbia-star-topic-takes-home-mvp-award |access-date=11 July 2026 |website=FIBA.basketball}}</ref>

González also represented Spain at the [[2024 FIBA U18 EuroBasket]], averaging 20.7 points, 6.9 rebounds and 2.6 assists over seven games.<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 August 2024 |title=Rising Stars: 10 players who made an impact at FIBA U18 EuroBasket |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-u18-eurobasket-2024/news/rising-stars-10-players-who-made-an-impact-at-fiba-u18-eurobasket |access-date=11 July 2026 |website=FIBA.basketball}}</ref>

===Senior team===
On 20 February 2025, González made his debut for the [[Spain men's national basketball team|senior Spanish national team]], scoring 11 points and collecting six rebounds in an 83–66 loss to [[Latvia men's national basketball team|Latvia]] during [[EuroBasket 2025 qualification]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=20 February 2025 |title=Hugo González makes his debut with the Spanish national team |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/basket/first-team/latest-news/hugo-gonzalez-debuta-con-la-seleccion-espanola-20-02-2025 |access-date=11 July 2026 |website=Real Madrid CF}}</ref>

He returned to the national team for two [[2027 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Europe)|2027 FIBA World Cup qualifying]] games in July 2026, averaging 12.5 points, 3.5 rebounds and 3.5 assists. In a 109–81 victory over Denmark on 2 July, González recorded 16 points, five rebounds and five assists.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hugo Gonzalez – Spain – Player Profile |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-basketball-world-cup-2027-european-qualifiers/teams/spain/300763-hugo-gonzalez |access-date=11 July 2026 |website=FIBA.basketball}}</ref>
